data.name: Nicodema
data.gender_notes: Nicodema is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Nicodemus means ‘victory of the people.’ In the New Testament, Nicodemus is a Pharisee and a secret disciple of Jesus. The name Nicodema carries the meaning “Victory of the people” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nicodema usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes transformation through the power of faith.
data.etymology: Nicodema belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory of the people.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nicodema total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: ניקודמא
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ניקודמא הוא שם יהודי-יווני, המשמר עז, גבורה וניצחון. בספרות תלמודית, ניקודמא הוא שם נפוץ, ומוזכר בבבא מציעא (24a) ובשבת (31a). שם זה נזכר גם בספר 'ספר היחסים' של רבי יהודה החסיד. במסורת הנוצרית, ניקודמא מיוחס לאחד מתלמידיו של ישו, ניקודימוס, שהיה רב-אמן (גבור) שהכיר את ישו.

in_greek.name: Νικόδημος
in_greek.meaning: νίκη, δύναμις, νίκη και ονομασία Εβραϊκού-Ελληνικού
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Νικόδημος είναι Εβραϊκό-Ελληνικό όνομα, που σημαίνει νίκη, δύναμις και νίκη. Στη Βυζαντινή εποχή, το όνομα Νικόδημος ήταν πολύ δημοφιλές και συσχετίζεται με την ελληνική λέξη νίκη. Στη Βίβλο, το όνομα Νικόδημος δεν προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή, αλλά από το ελληνικό. Ο Νικόδημος ήταν ιερέας από τον Βηθανία και ήταν παρών στις τελετές της εορτής των Πάσχα.

in_latin.name: Nicodema
in_latin.meaning: victoria, virtus, victoria et nomen Hebraico-Graecum
in_latin.long_meaning: Nicodema est nomen Hebraico-Graecum, quod significat victoria, virtus et victoria. In historia Ecclesiae, Nicodema erat nomen populare, et mentionatur in Codice Theodosianum (C. Th. 16, 8, 34). Nomen istud erat nomen viri virtutis et victoriae, qui fuit discipulus Iesu Christi.

in_english.name: Nicodema
in_english.meaning: victory, strength, and conqueror, a Jewish-Greek name
in_english.long_meaning: Nicodema is a Jewish-Greek name, meaning victory, strength, and conqueror. In biblical context, Nicodema is mentioned as a name of a Jewish leader who recognized Jesus as the Messiah. In Christian tradition, Nicodema is associated with Nicodemus, a Pharisee who became a follower of Jesus. The name Nicodema is also associated with the virtue of courage and strength, as it is derived from the Greek word 'nike', meaning victory.

celebrity_usage: Nicodemus, a Pharisee in the New Testament
data.cultural_impact: Nicodemus is a name that carries ancient cultural weight, rooted in the Hebrew language and tradition. In biblical times, the name represented the triumph of the collective Jewish community over adversity. Nicknamed “the teacher of Israel” for his profound understanding of the scriptures, Nicodemus was a Pharisee – a member of an influential religious and social group known for their strict adherence to Jewish customs and traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Nicodemus is most notably remembered for his meeting with Jesus in the New Testament. During this encounter, Jesus spoke to Nicodemus of the necessity of spiritual rebirth – a concept difficult for the Pharisee to fully grasp at first. Though initially reluctant to embrace Jesus' teachings, Nicodemus ultimately became a secret disciple, using his position and influence within the Jewish community to support and protect Jesus. Through this transformative encounter, Nicodemus came to embody the idea of spiritual renewal and the power of personal growth, even in the face of adversity. Thus, the name Nicodemus continues to hold a deeply spiritual significance, symbolizing the triumph of the human soul over worldly challenges and the profound potential for transformation that lies within us all.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nicodemus means "victory of the people of God" from the Hebrew name "Nicodemus," derived from "Nikodemos" or "Nikodemos," meaning "people of God" and "victory." This name symbolizes the triumph of faith and divine guidance in one's personal life and community.

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament, Nicodema was a Pharisee who helped Joseph of Arimathea prepare Jesus' body for burial.

trends: rarely used in modern times, but still used in some Christian contexts
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Nicodema remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Elizabeth Nicodema from Rome, Italy embodies the meaning of Nicodema - "Victory of the people". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
